subject: mathematics
question_text: If x is acute and sin(x + 10°) = cos(3x − 68°), find x in degrees.

mark_split.label: Take n odd and choose the acute value

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.109, chapter 9 TRIGONOMETRIC EQUATIONS, Short Answer question 6. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1+1+1 shape gives a mark to EACH parity of n, because the short route — assume both angles are acute and set their sum to 90° — reaches 37° without ever showing that the other family gives nothing acute, and that is the half of the question a 4-mark answer is expected to write. CANDIDATE RECORD: the even family gives x = 90m + 37, so 37° (acute, kept) and 127°, 217°, … (not acute); the odd family gives x = −180m − 6, so −6°, 174°, … (not acute). Every one of those satisfies the equation — they are rejected by the words 'x is acute', not by being extraneous, and the card says which kind of rejection it is. The answer was checked: sin47° = cos43° is true because 47° + 43° = 90°. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B prints eight short answers of which the student writes any six, each worth 4 marks, under the 2026-27 pattern; Trigonometric Equations supplies one of them. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — name each move in order, and say how the word 'acute' picks out the answer.

steps.label: Write both sides as sines
steps.margin_note: First mark. A sine cannot be compared with a cosine, so turn the cosine into a sine using cosA = sin(90° − A). Watch the double sign change on −68°.
steps.memory_tip: cosA = sin(90° − A). Subtracting −68° adds 68°, so the angle becomes 158° − 3x.

recall.must_convey: That cos(3x − 68°) is written as sin(158° − 3x), so both sides are sines.

steps.why: Two trigonometric expressions can only be equated angle-to-angle when they are the SAME function. Converting the cosine to a sine is what makes the comparison legal.
common_mistakes: Equating x + 10° with 3x − 68° directly, mixing sine with cosine.

steps.label: Apply the sine general solution
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Do not just equate the angles — write the full sine general solution in degrees, because both parities of n give real solutions and the question must choose between them.
steps.memory_tip: In degrees the sine general solution reads A = n(180°) + (−1)ⁿ B. Both parities of n matter here.

steps.why: sinA = sinB does not mean A = B. It means A belongs to a whole family of angles, and the two parities of n give two different equations in x.
common_mistakes: Writing A = B only and losing the second family.
Using π instead of 180° while the angles are in degrees.

steps.label: Take n even
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Put n = 2m so (−1)ⁿ = 1. Solving gives x = 90m + 37, and only m = 0 is acute.
steps.memory_tip: n even makes (−1)ⁿ = +1. Collect the x terms on one side: 4x = 360m + 148.
lines: If n is even, put n = 2m so (−1)ⁿ = 1.
All angles below are in degrees.
m = 0 gives x = 37°, which is acute.

recall.must_convey: That n even gives x = 90m + 37, and only m = 0 gives an acute value, x = 37°.

steps.why: With n even the sign is +1, and the three x terms collect into one linear equation. The family it produces is spaced 90° apart, so at most one member can be acute.
common_mistakes: Collecting 3x on the wrong side and getting 2x instead of 4x.
Dropping the 360m term so the family looks like a single value.

steps.label: Take n odd and choose the acute value
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Put n = 2m + 1 so (−1)ⁿ = −1. This family gives −6°, 174°, … — every one of them solves the equation, but none is acute, so the word 'acute' in the question is what selects 37°.
steps.memory_tip: n odd makes (−1)ⁿ = −1, so the bracket is subtracted. The family it gives has no acute member.
lines: If n is odd, put n = 2m + 1 so (−1)ⁿ = −1.
This gives −6°, 174°, … and none is acute.

recall.must_convey: That n odd gives x = −180m − 6, none of which is acute, so the acute answer is x = 37°.

steps.why: Both families are genuine solutions of the equation. They are not extraneous — the restriction 'x is acute' is what removes all of them but one, so the restriction has to be applied to BOTH families in writing.
common_mistakes: Answering 37° without ever testing the odd family.
Calling −6° a wrong answer instead of one the restriction removes.
Dropping the degree sign from the final answer.
